# ScriptServer

*Server*

Controls the Minecraft server and its optional voice groups from server scripts. Voice groups are identified by UUID; group operations run on the Minecraft server thread.

## Methods

### getMinecraftServer {#getminecraftserver}

::: member

**Returns** `MinecraftServer` — the Minecraft server, for Java code

:::

### getRegion {#getregion}

::: member

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | saved region name |

**Returns** [`ScramServerRegion`](/scripting/server/ScramServerRegion) — named region from regions.json, or null if absent; independent of loaded chunks

:::

### getRegions {#getregions}

::: member

**Returns** `List<ScramServerRegion>` — named regions across all dimensions, in catalog order

:::

### createRegion {#createregion}

::: member

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | new region name, 1..128 characters without control characters; must not already exist |
| `dimension` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | valid dimension identifier, e.g. minecraft:overworld |
| `first` | [`ScriptVector`](/scripting/common/ScriptVector) | first absolute corner, fractional, finite and within +/-30000000 |
| `second` | [`ScriptVector`](/scripting/common/ScriptVector) | second absolute corner with the same requirements; the region spans exactly between both corners |

**Returns** [`ScramServerRegion`](/scripting/server/ScramServerRegion) — created region, saved and synchronized immediately

:::

### createTrigger {#createtrigger}

::: member

Creates a trigger on a block, whose hitboxes follow the block's outline; make it a shape around a point with

[`setPoint`](/scripting/server/ScramServerTrigger#setpoint). Its click triggers are set in the functional editor.

```js
var button = c.getServer().createTrigger("button", "minecraft:overworld", 10, 64, 10);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | new trigger name, 1..128 characters without control characters; must not already exist |
| `dimension` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | dimension identifier, e.g. minecraft:overworld |
| `x` | [`int`](/scripting/js/Number) | block x |
| `y` | [`int`](/scripting/js/Number) | block y |
| `z` | [`int`](/scripting/js/Number) | block z |

**Returns** [`ScramServerTrigger`](/scripting/server/ScramServerTrigger) — created trigger, saved and synchronized immediately

:::

### getStates {#getstates}

::: member


::: member

| `id` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | display ID |

**Returns** [`ScriptServerDisplayForm`](/scripting/server/ScriptServerDisplayForm) — the shown display, or null if no display with this ID is shown

:::

### getVoiceGroup {#getvoicegroup}

::: member

Gets a snapshot of a registered voice group's properties. The returned map does not update when the group changes or is removed.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uuid` | `UUID` | the group UUID, not null |

**Returns** `Map<String,Any>` — an immutable map with uuid, name, hasPassword, hidden, persistent and type (normal, open or isolated), or null if no such group exists

:::

### getVoiceGroupId {#getvoicegroupid}

::: member

Finds the first voice group with an exact, case sensitive name. Names are not necessarily unique.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | the group name, not null |

**Returns** `UUID` — the group UUID, or null if no group has that name

:::

### createVoiceGroup {#createvoicegroup}

::: member

Creates a normal, visible voice group without a password and with a random UUID. The group is removed when its last member leaves. Call it on the Minecraft server thread.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | the nonblank group name, not null |

**Returns** `UUID` — the created group UUID, or null if another plugin cancels creation

:::

### createVoiceGroup {#createvoicegroup-2}

::: member

Creates a voice group using named options, for example:

```js
ctx.getServer().createVoiceGroup("phone", {hidden: true, persistent: true, type: "isolated"});
```

Call it on the Minecraft server thread. Missing options use the defaults below.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | the nonblank group name, not null |
| `options` | `Map<String,Any>` | a JavaScript object or Java map, or null for defaults: uuid (UUID or UUID string, random by default), password (string or null, no password by default; an empty string also disables the password), hidden (boolean, false by default), persistent (boolean, false by default; true retains an empty group until server shutdown), type (normal, open or isolated, ignoring case; null or omitted selects normal). Normal groups send microphone audio to the group and hear the group plus nearby players; open groups send and hear both group and proximity audio; isolated groups only send and hear the group. Options are not modified, and groups are not saved across server restarts. |

**Returns** `UUID` — the created group UUID, or null if another plugin cancels creation

:::

### getEntities {#getentities}

::: member

Finds entities with a target selector as the server console would; positions are relative to the world spawn.

```js
for (var cow of c.getServer().getEntities("@e[type=minecraft:cow]")) {
    cow.kill();
}
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `selector` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | target selector like `"@a[gamemode=survival]"`, a player name or a UUID |

**Returns** `List<ScriptServerEntity<?>>` — matching entities

:::

### executeScript {#executescript}

::: member

Runs the `main` function of a server script without a subject.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `script` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | script ID; a missing script does nothing |

**Returns** `Any` — what the function returned: strings, numbers, booleans and Java objects as they are, JavaScript arrays as lists and objects as maps; null if it returned nothing, or the script or function does not exist

:::

### executeScript {#executescript-2}

::: member

Runs a function of a server script without a subject, in the same tick; its world is the overworld.

```js
// utils/prices: function get(c) { return {sword: 10, bow: 5}; }
var prices = c.getServer().executeScript("utils/prices", "get");

c.send("A sword costs " + prices.get("sword"));
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `script` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | script ID; a missing script does nothing |
| `function` | [`String`](/scripting/js/String) | function name |

**Returns** `Any` — what the function returned: strings, numbers, booleans and Java objects as they are, JavaScript arrays as lists and objects as maps; null if it returned nothing, or the script or function does not exist

:::
